newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian government buys stake in broadcast firm.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian government buys stake in broadcast firm.

text.p: The Malaysian government's investment arm, Khazanah Nasional Bhd, has acquired a 15 percent stake in a company licensed to provide satellite broadcast services, the national Bernama news agency said on Monday.
Bernama quoted a Khazanah statement as saying the stake in Measat Broadcast Network Systems Sdn Bhd is its first in the multimedia and information technology sector.
Measat Broadcast plans to provide 20 video channels, as well as multiple satellite and terrestrial radio channels, to Malaysia, India and the Philippines.
Khazanah, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Minister of Finance Inc, did not give financial details of the deal. Khazanah officials could not immediately be contacted for comment.

Measat Broadcast was the first company to locate in Malaysia's newly launched "Multimedia Super Corridor", a 15-km by 50-km zone that stretches from Kuala Lumpur south to a new international airport and federal capital under construction. The zone aims to attract global information technology companies.
Measat Broadcast is a subsidiary of Binariang Sdn Bhd, which launched Malaysia's first communications satellite in January.
